question:
A family of curves has the property that at every point $(x,y)$ on a curve, with $x\neq0$ and $y\neq0$, the slope of the tangent is $\frac{x^2+y^2}{2xy}$. Students are asked to determine the equation of the entire family of curves from this slope condition. They observe that after dividing the numerator and denominator by $x^2$, the slope can be expressed completely in terms of the ratio $\frac{y}{x}$. This makes it possible to treat the relation as a homogeneous differential equation and obtain the family represented by an arbitrary constant.

(a) Write the differential equation representing the given tangent-slope condition and show that its right-hand side depends only on $\frac{y}{x}$.

(b) Put $y=vx$ and reduce the differential equation to an equation involving $v$ and $x$.

(c) Separate the variables and integrate the reduced equation.

(d) Show that the resulting family of curves can be written as $x^2-y^2=Cx$.
explanation:
(a)
The slope of the tangent is $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Therefore, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x^2+y^2}{2xy}$$

Dividing the numerator and denominator on the right-hand side by $x^2$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1+\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^2}{2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}$$

Thus the right-hand side depends only on $\frac{y}{x}$, so the differential equation is homogeneous.

(b)
Put $y=vx$. Then, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$$

Substituting in the differential equation, $$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1+v^2}{2v}$$

Therefore, $$x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1-v^2}{2v}$$

(c)
Separating the variables, $$\frac{2v}{1-v^2}\,dv=\frac{dx}{x}$$

Integrating, $$\int\frac{2v}{1-v^2}\,dv=\int\frac{dx}{x}$$

Hence, $$-\log|1-v^2|=\log|x|+C_1$$

Equivalently, $$\log|x(1-v^2)|=C_2$$

Therefore, $$x(1-v^2)=C$$ where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

(d)
Since $v=\frac{y}{x}$, $$x\left(1-\frac{y^2}{x^2}\right)=C$$

Thus, $$\frac{x^2-y^2}{x}=C$$

Multiplying by $x$, $$x^2-y^2=Cx$$

Hence the required family of curves is $x^2-y^2=Cx$.

options.C:
(a) The right side is not a function of $\frac{y}{x}$
(b) $x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1-v}{2v}$
(c) $\frac{2v}{1-v}\,dv=\frac{dx}{x}$
(d) $x-y=Cx$
